text:
kevin: heads up — noticed a weird billing spike on a customer call. they did a streaming generation, then mid-stream the client invoked a toolcall. during a canary model swap the session replayed and i think the prefix got counted twice. anyone seen this exact combo? 😬

maria: yikes. any logs? which model swap path — fallback to smaller model or canary rollforward?

kevin: fallback path. basic repro: client starts stream -> server sends tokens -> client triggers toolcall -> we pause streaming and route toolcall to tool-runner -> toolcall returns -> we resume streaming but the router switched to canary instance because of capacity. result: ledger shows original prefix + resumed prefix as separate billable prefixes.

alex: can you paste the minimal trace? even a snip of the router trace and ledger lines helps.

kevin: sure, grabbed the span ids:
```
router.trace: span=span_23a id=4943216789 route=primary->canary at=2026-03-19T15:12:10Z
session.resume: session_id=sess_7a prefix_len=48 resumed_from=canary instance=canary-3
billing.event: token_bucket_debit session=sess_7a amount=48 meta=prefix_start
billing.event: token_bucket_debit session=sess_7a amount=48 meta=resume_prefix
```

kevin: note the two debits with identical amounts.

ops-bot: automated note: recent deploy (canary routing v2) rolled out at 2026-03-19T15:11:58Z.

ben: hmm looks like resume path created a new prefix owner record rather than extending the original. we probably key prefixes by (session, instance_id) now, not just session+prefix-hash.

maria: that would explain duplicate debits. the original prefix belonged to primary-2, resume recorded to canary-3. accounting currently treats those as distinct and bills both.

alex: is this limited to cases where toolcall interrupts streaming? or any midstream model swap?

kevin: repro seems deterministic only when a toolcall causes routing decision (tool-runner affinity -> different capacity pool). normal model swap without toolcall hasn't shown dupes yet.

sophie: UX question: for Console billing view, do we surface both debits or consolidate? right now dashboards show both and SRE gets paged by customers.

ben: i'd prefer we consolidate at ledger-reconciliation: detect contiguous debits within Xs that sum to same prefix length and collapse to single charge if session ids match and tokens overlap. but need to be careful for legitimate reruns.

maria: tradeoffs: collapsing hides real double-work when clients legitimately re-requested text. customers will want transparency. maybe mark consolidated entries with "inferred-merge" and keep raw events in audit log.

alex: engineering impl note: easier fix might be routing layer: when resuming a session, attempt to claim previous prefix owner if still present (try-steal with TTL). if not, record mapping (old_owner->new_owner) and emit a reconciliation marker so billing can attribute to original owner.

kevin: agreed. quick patch: on resume, attach header `X-previous-prefix-owner: <owner>` to resume RPC so billing can join records. fallback to reconciliation if header missing.

ben: that header approach looks low-risk. add a unit test in router that simulates toolcall-induced route flip and asserts single prefix attribution header included.

ops-bot: perf note: adding header increases RPC small, acceptable per canary perf tests.

maria: i'll open a short-lived spike PR to add header + ledger join heuristic. also update console to tag merged rows with orange flag and tooltip explaining merge reason.

kevin: thanks. created a short repro script and attached to PR: `scripts/repro/4943_toolcall-resume.sh`. will link in PR.

sophie: and can we add a telemetry counter: `billing.prefix_attribution.duplicates_detected` and `billing.prefix_attribution.merged` so we can track fix efficacy?

ben: yep. add both counters and a dashboard panel under "Billing -> Token anomalies". threshold alert if duplicates > 1% of prefix events for an account.

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/842 — includes header, unit test, and dashboard checkout.

kevin: verified repro against the branch, duplicates stop once header flows. marking this thread resolved for now, will monitor. :thumbsup:

alex: great. follow-up: we should schedule a short retro to decide long-term model for prefix ownership across routing domains (single global prefix ledger vs per-instance).

kevin: +1, thanks everyone.
